summary_for_children: Al-Mujadila means The Pleading Woman. It begins with Allah hearing a woman who complained to Him, and teaches making room for others in gatherings and seeking knowledge.
environment_concept: An open hall where room is made for others (58:11), with seats in a circle and houses around.
architecture_and_scenery: A simple hall with mats, room that expands when people make space.

areas.name: The Hall
areas.description: A hall that expands as space is made.

activities.name: Make space
activities.description: Carry six cushions to make room in the circle.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Allah hears
activities.description: Read 58:1 and discuss how Allah hears every request.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Woman Who Was Heard
story_library.children_narration: A woman brought a serious concern about unfair treatment in her marriage to Prophet Muhammad. The Quran tells us that Allah heard her complaint. Her story reminds us that people's concerns matter and that unfairness should not be ignored.

world_idea.title: The Hall of Listening
world_idea.description: Explore a respectful council environment and practice listening carefully to fictional community concerns. The original historical event is conveyed through narration, not acted out by invented characters.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The woman and the Prophet are not shown; the hall uses fictional concerns, labelled.
